reviewed_by: claude-opus-5 blind reviewer, re-review after the distance-clause fixes, 2026-08-13

samples_reviewed.question_text: An object measures 11 cm. About how many cm is that, rounded to the nearest 5?
The distance from the gate to the flagpole is 11 m. About how many m is that, rounded to the nearest 5?
The distance from the gate to the flagpole is 18 m. About how many m is that, rounded to the nearest 5?
The distance from the gate to the flagpole is 16 m. About how many m is that, rounded to the nearest 5?
An object measures 13 cm. About how many cm is that, rounded to the nearest 5?
The distance from the gate to the flagpole is 11 m. About how many m is that, rounded to the nearest 5?
An object measures 487 cm. About how many cm is that, rounded to the nearest 50?
An object measures 322 cm. About how many cm is that, rounded to the nearest 50?
An object measures 87 cm. About how many cm is that, rounded to the nearest 10?
An object measures 12 cm. About how many cm is that, rounded to the nearest 5?
The distance from the gate to the flagpole is 19 m. About how many m is that, rounded to the nearest 5?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Every item demands a real rounding judgment and in no sample is the answer already the stated value. Seed 42 asks 'An object measures 11 cm. About how many cm is that, rounded to the nearest 5?' and answers 10; seed 46 turns 13 into 15, seed 500 turns 487 into 500, and seed 44 turns 18 into 20. The distance half is expressed in the unit the competency requires, as at seed 43 with 'The distance from the gate to the flagpole is 11 m.'

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Looking for each part of the sentence separately: estimating distance in meters is well covered by seeds 43, 44, 45, 50 and 601, the last reading 'The distance from the gate to the flagpole is 19 m.', and estimating length in centimeters is covered by seeds 42, 46, 500, 501, 502 and 600. The meter option of the length clause never appears, as no seed estimates the length of an object in m, so two of the three unit-and-quantity pairings the sentence permits are exercised and one is absent across eleven samples.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Rounding grains of 5, 10 and 50 are each a single benchmark decision rather than a procedure, as at seed 502 with 'An object measures 87 cm. About how many cm is that, rounded to the nearest 10?'. The largest number, 487, remains inside the Grade 2 whole-number range, and distractors sit one or two units away so the choice turns on the benchmark rather than on careless reading.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Two stem families appear, object length and gate-to-flagpole distance, across two formatters, with three rounding grains: nearest 5 at seed 45, nearest 10 at seed 502, and nearest 50 at seed 501 with 'An object measures 322 cm. About how many cm is that, rounded to the nearest 50?'. Direction varies as well, since seed 44 rounds 18 up to 20 while seed 45 rounds 16 down to 15, so a student cannot pass by always rounding the same way.

competency_alignment.rationale: Every stem is genuinely an estimation stem, putting its question as 'About how many', and none drifts into exact measurement, comparison or unit conversion. The distance items use meters exactly as the sentence directs, and no stem prints an internal placeholder instead of a unit or an object name.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The small items are entirely plausible, such as the 12 cm object at seed 600 and the 16 m walk at seed 45. The large ones are not: seed 500 states 'An object measures 487 cm.' and seed 501 states 'An object measures 322 cm.', describing objects of nearly five meters and over three meters reported in centimeters, a magnitude no Grade 2 child obtains from a cm ruler, and the competency itself supplies meters for lengths of that size.
